body:
It _does_ in fact round to step, but the step isn't what you expect, due to [floating-point inaccuracy](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/588004/is-floating-point-math-broken). The number 0.1 is not perfectly representable as a float, so it'll be something like 0.10000001... instead. So the rounded values are -1.0, -0.89999999..., ..., -0.0999999..., 0.0000001... and so on.

It's unfortunate, and perhaps unexpected, that 0 is not among these values, even if it can be represented perfectly — but I'm not sure there is a general way to solve this.

It happens to work if the minimum value is 0, because then you get 0 * 0.10000001... which is exactly 0.

I suggest you write your shader to take this into account, by not comparing `spread == 0.0` but rather something like `abs(spread) < EPSILON` for a suitably small value of `EPSILON`.

> It's unfortunate, and perhaps unexpected, that 0 is not among these values, even if it can be represented perfectly — but I'm not sure there is a general way to solve this.

I think maybe 0 deserves some special treatment then, but I see how that is hard to decide and probably heavily based on preference.

> It happens to work if the minimum value is 0, because then you get 0 * 0.10000001... which is exactly 0.

It's just really unintuitive that it is exactly 0 until you change the value in the inspector once, but I guess you can revert it by manually changing the `.tscn` file and remove the non-default value.
